actOrScheme: Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023
authority: Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS), Ministry of Cooperation
title: Active Member Disqualification and Voting Rights
content: No member of a multi-state co-operative society shall exercise voting rights in general body meetings (AGM) or board elections unless they have attended at least three consecutive general meetings and utilized the minimum level of products or services of the society as specified in the registered bye-laws.

actOrScheme: Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023
authority: Co-operative Election Authority, Government of India
title: Autonomous Co-operative Election Authority
content: The Central Government establishes an autonomous body known as the Co-operative Election Authority to conduct elections of the board of multi-state co-operative societies in a free, fair, transparent, and timely manner, preventing arbitrary postponement of democratic elections.

actOrScheme: Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023
authority: Co-operative Ombudsman, Ministry of Cooperation
title: Co-operative Ombudsman for Redressal of Member Complaints
content: The Central Government appoints Co-operative Ombudsmen with territorial jurisdiction to inquire into grievances filed by members against multi-state co-operative societies regarding non-repayment of fixed deposits, refusal of shares, denial of dividends, or corruption. Form VI is prescribed for complaints and Form VII for appeals, with a statutory resolution window of 30 days.

actOrScheme: Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023
authority: Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS)
title: Members Right to Inspect Society Accounts & Audit Reports
content: Every member of a co-operative society has the statutory right to inspect audited balance sheets, profit and loss statements, list of members, registered bye-laws, and minutes of general meetings upon submitting an application to the society secretary.

actOrScheme: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) Operational Guidelines
authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, GoI
title: 72-Hour Mandatory Calamity Loss Intimation Rule
content: In the event of localized natural calamities (such as hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst, or post-harvest cyclone damage within 14 days of harvest), the insured farmer MUST intimate crop loss within 72 hours via the Crop Insurance App, national toll-free helpline 14447, or the nearest PACS/Agriculture Office for survey and direct DBT compensation.

actOrScheme: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) Premium Schedule
authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, GoI
title: Subsidized Farmer Premium Rates & Government Subsidy Sharing
content: Uniform maximum premium payable by farmers: 2.0% of Sum Insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% of Sum Insured for Rabi food and oilseed crops, and 5.0% for commercial or horticultural crops. The entire balance actuarial premium (often 12% to 18%) is shared 50:50 by the Central and State Governments as direct subsidy.

actOrScheme: PMFBY Technology Integration Framework
authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
title: YES-TECH, WINDS & CROPIC Remote Sensing Architecture
content: PMFBY deploys YES-TECH (Yield Estimation System using satellite and drone remote sensing), WINDS (Weather Information Network and Data System deploying village-level automatic weather stations), and CROPIC (geotagged farmer smartphone photographs) to ensure transparent, automated, and tamper-proof claim settlement.

actOrScheme: Model By-Laws for Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS)
authority: Ministry of Cooperation & NABARD
title: Diversification of PACS into 25+ Economic and Citizen Services
content: Empowers functional PACS across India to diversify beyond short-term crop credit into 25+ business lines, including Pradhan Mantri Jan Aushadhi Kendras (with ₹5 Lakh grant assistance for generic medicines), Custom Hiring Machinery & Drone Centers, Fair Price Shops, Common Service Centers (CSCs) providing 300+ e-services, and bio-fertilizer distribution.

actOrScheme: Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS
authority: Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India
title: ₹2,925.39 Cr Cloud ERP Mission Covering 79,630 PACS
content: The Central Government expanded the computerization mission to cover 79,630 PACS with an approved financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 Crore. Over 63,686 PACS are onboarded to the unified National Cloud ERP software, with over 54,707 operating as e-PACS, directly linked to District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs).

actOrScheme: Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) on Short-Term Crop Loans
authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) & Ministry of Agriculture
title: 4% Effective Net Interest Rate on Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
content: Short-term crop credit up to ₹3.00 Lakh is available to farmers at a benchmark lending rate of 9%. The Central Government provides a 2% upfront interest subvention (reducing rate to 7%), and an additional 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) for farmers who repay within due date, resulting in an effective net interest rate of only 4.0% per annum.

actOrScheme: Agricultural Credit and Infrastructure Policy
authority: NABARD and Ministry of Agriculture
title: Collateral-Free Credit Limits and Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
content: Institutional crop loans up to Rs 1.60 Lakh (extended to Rs 2.00 Lakh in functional computerized PACS) require zero land mortgage or collateral security. Under the Rs 1 Lakh Crore Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), PACS can build village cold storage and warehouses with a 3% interest subvention on loans up to Rs 2.00 Crore for 7 years.

actOrScheme: National Cooperative Seed Policy
authority: Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India
title: Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) - Certified Seeds
content: BBSSL is an apex multi-state cooperative established by IFFCO, KRIBHCO, NAFED, NDDB, and NCDC to cultivate, certify, test, and distribute high-yielding certified indigenous seeds through PACS across India, boosting agricultural productivity and preserving heritage varieties.

actOrScheme: National Cooperative Organic Farming Mission
authority: Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India
title: National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) - Bharat Organics
content: NCOL is the national apex cooperative society marketing verified organic products under the Bharat Organics brand. It establishes laboratory networks, ensures certified organic standards, and provides farmers premium prices for chemical-free crops without middleman cuts.

actOrScheme: National Cooperative Export Promotion Framework
authority: Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India
title: National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) - Global Trade
content: NCEL acts as an umbrella body promoting the export of agricultural produce, dairy, handloom, and cooperative products to international markets. Profits from global export contracts are distributed directly back to primary producers and cooperative members.

actOrScheme: National Council for Cooperative Training (NCCT) Charter
authority: National Council for Cooperative Training, Ministry of Cooperation
sectionOrClause: Cooperative Education and Human Resource Development
title: NCCT and VAMNICOM Cooperative Management Training Programmes
content: NCCT and its apex institution VAMNICOM (Vaikunth Mehta National Institute of Cooperative Management, Pune) operate 14 Regional Institutes (RICMs) and 5 Institutes of Cooperative Management (ICMs). They offer Higher Diploma in Cooperative Management (HDCM), PGDM in Agri-Business, and executive training for PACS secretaries, board directors, and cooperative auditors.

actOrScheme: White Revolution 2.0 and National Dairy Expansion
authority: Ministry of Cooperation and National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)
title: White Revolution 2.0 - Dairy Cooperatives in 2 Lakh Panchayats
content: White Revolution 2.0 aims to establish viable multi-purpose primary dairy cooperative societies in 2 Lakh uncovered Gram Panchayats. Supported by NDDB and State Milk Federations, it installs Automatic Milk Collection Units (AMCUs), micro-chilling centers, and connects rural women to regular direct-to-bank milk payments.

actOrScheme: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
authority: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
sectionOrClause: National Women SHG Economic Empowerment Framework
title: Lakhpati Didi Initiative for Rural Women Self-Help Groups
content: The Lakhpati Didi initiative aims to empower 3 Crore rural women associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to earn a sustainable annual household income of at least Rs 1 Lakh through diversified livelihoods, enterprise training, market linkages, interest-subvention credit, and community investment funds.

actOrScheme: Central Sector Scheme for Financial Assistance to Women SHGs for Drones
authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Chemicals/Fertilizers
title: NaMo Drone Didi Scheme - 80% Subsidy on Agricultural Drones
content: Provides 15,000 selected women Self-Help Groups with agricultural drones for rental services (spraying nano urea, liquid DAP, pesticides). The scheme provides 80% financial assistance (up to Rs 8 Lakh) towards the drone package cost and provides 15 days of certified pilot training with stipend.

actOrScheme: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Act No. 22 of 2005)
authority: Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) and Central Information Commission (CIC)
title: Right to Information (RTI) Online Filing and 30-Day SLA
content: Under the RTI Act 2005, every Indian citizen can seek information from any public authority. File online at rtionline.gov.in with a Rs 10 fee (free for BPL cardholders). The Public Information Officer (PIO) must respond within 30 days (within 48 hours if life and liberty is concerned). First Appeal lies to the FAA and Second Appeal to the Information Commission.

actOrScheme: Representation of the People Act, 1950 and Registration of Electors Rules
authority: Election Commission of India (ECI)
title: Voter Registration, EPIC Download and National Voter Services Portal
content: Citizens aged 18+ can register as new voters using Form 6 on voters.eci.gov.in or the Voter Helpline App. Form 8 is used for correction of entries or shifting of residence. Digital Voter ID (e-EPIC) can be downloaded instantly using registered mobile number. National Helpline: 1950.

actOrScheme: Information Technology Rules
authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
title: DigiLocker - Legally Valid Digital Document Wallet
content: Documents issued via DigiLocker (Driving License, Vehicle RC, Aadhaar, PAN, Ration Card, Marksheets) are deemed legally equivalent to physical original documents under Rule 9A of the IT Rules. Provides 1 GB secure cloud storage linked to Aadhaar.

actOrScheme: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
authority: Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), MeitY
title: Aadhaar Services: Changing Email & Mobile, Address Update, PVC Card & 1947 Helpline
content: UIDAI provides the 12-digit Aadhaar unique identity. Key citizen procedures: (1) Changing/Updating Email ID & Mobile Number: For security, mobile number and email CANNOT be changed purely online without biometrics. Citizens must visit an Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK), authorized Bank, Post Office, or use IPPB doorstep service. Fee is Rs 50. No document is required; only biometric (fingerprint/iris) authentication is taken. Appointments can be booked at appointments.uidai.gov.in. (2) Address Update: Can be done 100% online on myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in with valid address proof (or Head of Family HoF consent). (3) Download e-Aadhaar PDF: Download from myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in (password is first 4 letters of name in CAPITAL + birth year). (4) PVC Card: Order online for Rs 50 delivered via Speed Post. (5) Biometric Lock/Unlock: Free on mAadhaar app to prevent AePS fraud. National 24x7 Helpline: 1947 | help@uidai.gov.in.

actOrScheme: Income-tax Act, 1961 and Income-tax Rules, 1962
authority: Income Tax Department & Protean (NSDL) / UTIITSL
title: PAN Card Services: New PAN, Correction, Instant e-PAN & Aadhaar Linking
content: A 10-digit alphanumeric identifier issued by the Income Tax Department. (1) New PAN Application: File Form 49A online on Protean (tin-nsdl.com) or UTIITSL (pan.utiitsl.com). Fee is Rs 107 for physical dispatch in India, Rs 72 for e-PAN. (2) Instant e-PAN: 100% Free digital PAN generated in 10 minutes using Aadhaar e-KYC on incometax.gov.in. (3) Linking PAN with Aadhaar: Mandatory under Section 139AA via incometax.gov.in portal. (4) Correction/Update: Submit PAN Change Request form on NSDL/UTIITSL. Helpline: 1800-180-1961.

actOrScheme: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended) and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989
authority: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) & State RTOs
title: Parivahan Sarathi: Driving Licence, Learner Licence & Vehicle RC Services
content: Administered via Parivahan Sewa (sarathi.parivahan.gov.in). (1) Learner's Licence (LL): Apply online with Aadhaar authentication; take computer learner test from home without visiting RTO in most states. (2) Permanent Driving Licence (DL): Apply after 30 days of LL and within 6 months. Book driving test slot at designated RTO. (3) Renewal & Address Change: Apply online via Sarathi with Form 9 and Form 1-A medical certificate (for age 40+). (4) Vahan Portal (vahan.parivahan.gov.in): Vehicle RC transfer, fitness, and hypothecation removal. Helpline: 0120-4925505.

actOrScheme: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 & State Citizen Service Delivery Acts
authority: Registrar General of India & State Revenue / e-District Departments
title: Citizen Certificates: Birth, Death, Caste, Income & Domicile Registration
content: Official government certificates issued via National CRS (crsorgi.gov.in) and State e-District portals (e.g. Aaple Sarkar Maharashtra, e-District UP/Delhi/Bihar, MeeSeva, Seva Sindhu). (1) Birth & Death Certificate: Free registration within 21 days of occurrence at municipal ward or Gram Panchayat; digitally signed certificates downloaded from crsorgi.gov.in. (2) Income Certificate: Issued by Tehsildar/Sub-Divisional Magistrate for fee concessions and scholarships (valid 1 to 3 financial years). Requires Talathi report / ITR / Salary slip. (3) Caste & Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) Certificate: Issued for affirmative action; requires genealogical proof and pre-prescribed year residence proof (e.g., 1961/1967). (4) Domicile/Residence Certificate: Proof of continuous 15-year residency.

actOrScheme: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
authority: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Ministry of Labour and Employment
title: EPFO Member Portal: Check PF Balance, UAN Activation & Online Withdrawal Claims
content: EPFO manages retirement savings for formal sector employees. (1) Check Balance: Give a missed call to 9966044425 from registered mobile, send SMS 'EPFOHO UAN' to 7738299899, or view passbook at passbook.epfindia.gov.in. (2) Online PF Withdrawal (unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in): Form 19 (Final PF settlement after leaving job), Form 10C (Pension EPS withdrawal), Form 31 (Non-refundable Advance for medical, house purchase, marriage, or construction). (3) UAN Activation: Link active mobile, Aadhaar, and bank account with verified IFSC. Claims settled via DBT within 7 to 14 days. National Helpline: 1800-118-005.

actOrScheme: Passports Act, 1967
authority: CPV Division, Ministry of External Affairs, GoI
title: Passport Seva Online Application and Appointment Procedure
content: Citizens apply for normal or tatkaal passport online at passportindia.gov.in or mPassport Seva App. Book appointments at nearest Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) or Post Office Passport Seva Kendra (POPSK). Requires Proof of Birth, Address, and Aadhaar. National Helpline: 1800-258-1800.

actOrScheme: Short-Term Rural Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS)
authority: NABARD and Ministry of Cooperation
sectionOrClause: Banking Regulation Act and State Co-op Societies Acts
title: Three-Tier Rural Cooperative Credit Hierarchy (PACS - DCCB - StCB)
content: The Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure functions across three democratic tiers: Village Level (Primary Agricultural Credit Societies - PACS), District Level (District Central Cooperative Banks - DCCBs), and State Level (State Cooperative Banks - StCBs), refinanced by NABARD for concessional seasonal agricultural operations.

actOrScheme: The Patents Act, 1970 (as amended by Patents Amendment Rules 2024)
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
title: The Patents Act, 1970 – Patent Grant, Terms, Exclusions and Rights in India
content: The Patents Act, 1970 (Act No. 39 of 1970) governs the grant, protection, and enforcement of patents for inventions across India. An invention must satisfy novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability. Key provisions include: (1) Section 3 exclusions: non-patentable subject matter including Section 3(d) preventing mere discovery or evergreening of known pharmaceutical substances, Section 3(k) computer programs per se or mathematical algorithms, Section 3(b) inventions contrary to public order or morality, and Section 3(j) plants and animals; (2) Term of Patent: Under Section 53, every granted patent is valid for a statutory term of 20 years from the date of filing; (3) Exclusive Rights: Section 48 confers exclusive monopoly rights to prevent third parties from unauthorized making, using, offering for sale, selling, or importing the patented product or process; (4) Compulsory Licensing: Sections 84 and 92 allow compulsory licenses after 3 years if reasonable public requirements or fair pricing are unmet; (5) Filing Procedure: Applications are filed via Form 1 (Application for Grant of Patent) and Form 2 (Provisional/Complete Specification) on the official IP India portal (ipindia.gov.in) with up to 80% official fee concessions for Startups, MSMEs, and educational institutions.

actOrScheme: The Trade Marks Act, 1999 (Act No. 47 of 1999)
authority: Trade Marks Registry, CGPDTM, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
title: The Trade Marks Act, 1999 – Brand Protection, Registration and Infringement
content: The Trade Marks Act, 1999 provides statutory protection for distinctive brand names, logos, symbols, slogans, and 3D shapes distinguishing goods and services across 45 NICE classes. Registration gives the proprietor exclusive rights under Section 28 and legal remedy against infringement under Section 29. A registered trade mark is valid for 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely every 10 years via Form TM-R. e-Filing is processed on ipindiaonline.gov.in.

actOrScheme: The Copyright Act, 1957 (as amended by Copyright Amendment Act 2012)
authority: Copyright Office, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
title: The Copyright Act, 1957 – Protection of Literary, Artistic, Musical & Software Works
content: The Copyright Act, 1957 protects original literary, dramatic, musical, artistic works, cinematograph films, sound recordings, and computer software code. Copyright protection subsists automatically upon creation, while formal registration with the Copyright Office provides prima facie proof in court. The term of copyright for literary, musical, and artistic works is the lifetime of the author plus 60 years after their demise. E-filing portal is copyright.gov.in.

actOrScheme: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act No. 35 of 2019)
authority: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
title: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 – Consumer Rights, E-Daakhil and NCH 1915
content: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the 1986 Act, establishing the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to enforce consumer rights against unfair trade practices, misleading advertisements, and product liability. Pecuniary jurisdictions: District Commission up to Rs 50 Lakh, State Commission Rs 50 Lakh to Rs 2 Crore, National Commission (NCDRC) above Rs 2 Crore. Consumers can file complaints online via the e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) or call National Consumer Helpline 1915.

actOrScheme: The Information Technology Act, 2000 (as amended by IT Amendment Act 2008)
authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) & CERT-In
title: The Information Technology Act, 2000 – Cyber Law, Digital Signatures and Cyber Crime
content: The Information Technology Act, 2000 provides legal recognition to electronic records, digital signatures, and e-commerce transactions. Penalizes hacking (Sec 66), identity theft (Sec 66C), cheating by personation (Sec 66D), violation of bodily privacy (Sec 66E), cyber terrorism (Sec 66F), and failure to protect sensitive personal data (Sec 43A). Section 79 provides safe harbor to digital intermediaries complying with due diligence rules. Cyber complaints can be lodged on cybercrime.gov.in or helpline 1930.

actOrScheme: The Companies Act, 2013 (Act No. 18 of 2013)
authority: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), Government of India
title: The Companies Act, 2013 – Company Incorporation, Corporate Governance and CSR
content: The Companies Act, 2013 regulates the incorporation, governance, audit, and winding up of companies in India. Key features include: single-window incorporation via SPICe+ web form on MCA21 portal; mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR under Section 135) for eligible companies (2% of average net profits); independent directors (Sec 149); National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA); and Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO).

actOrScheme: Constitution of India – Fundamental Rights & Constitutional Remedies
authority: Supreme Court of India & High Courts, Ministry of Law & Justice
title: Fundamental Rights and Constitutional Remedies under the Constitution of India
content: Part III of the Constitution of India guarantees Fundamental Rights to all citizens: Article 14 (Right to Equality before law), Article 19 (Protection of freedoms including speech, expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and trade), Article 21 (Protection of Life and Personal Liberty including privacy), Article 21A (Right to Free & Compulsory Education for children 6-14), and Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies, declared the heart and soul of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar). Under Articles 32 and 226, citizens can move the Supreme Court and High Courts directly for issuing prerogative writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari).

actOrScheme: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006
authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), Government of India
title: MSME Udyam Registration: Free Paperless MSME Certificate & Enterprise Benefits
content: Administered via the official portal udyamregistration.gov.in. (1) 100% Free & Paperless: Zero fee, no agent, and no physical documentation required; only Aadhaar number of the proprietor/director and PAN are needed (linked with GSTIN). (2) Enterprise Classification: Micro (Investment <= 1 Cr & Turnover <= 5 Cr), Small (Investment <= 10 Cr & Turnover <= 50 Cr), Medium (Investment <= 50 Cr & Turnover <= 250 Cr). (3) Key Citizen & Business Benefits: Collateral-free loans under CGTMSE, priority sector lending, 50% concession on patent and trademark government filing fees, statutory protection against delayed payments (MSMED Act Section 15-16 compound interest), and government e-Marketplace (GeM) integration. National MSME Helpline: 011-23063288 / champions@gov.in.
